title: Gartner says agent costs will rise fivefold by 2028 even as tokens get cheaper. Here is how to keep them in check
key_facts: Gartner forecasts the cost of agentic AI workflows will increase more than fivefold by the end of 2028.
Falling model prices tempt users to build more complex workflows whose greater token use can outweigh the savings and push total inference costs up.
Will Sommer, a Gartner senior director analyst, contrasts a simple chatbot with an AI agent that 'must constantly reason, negotiate, and question itself'.
Routing a task to an agentic reasoning model increases inference costs at least fivefold, and potentially much more as tasks get more complex.
Gartner says the answer is more return or better optimisation of inference, routing and orchestration, such as assigning each task to the most cost-efficient capable model.
Some AI providers moving from flat-rate subscriptions to usage-based billing has not helped, per The Register.
quote_evidence: The cost of agentic AI workflows is forecast to increase more than fivefold by the end of 2028 as users adopt more complex applications of the technology.
Gartner believes falling model prices are tempting users to build more complex workflows, whose greater token consumption can outweigh those savings and drive up overall inference costs.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheaper tokens do not mean cheaper AI agents; heavier use may outrun the savings, according to Gartner's forecast.
notes: Older news re-dated: the forecast is from 17 Aug 2026; VentureBeat re-reported it on 16 Oct 2026.
